newsitem.title: USA: Case reports 21 percent jump in earnings.
newsitem.headline: Case reports 21 percent jump in earnings.

text.p: Case Corp. said Thursday its earnings jumped 21 percent in the first quarter, with the increase led by gains in sales of agricultural and construction equipment overseas.
The Racine, Wis.-based company said it earned $62 million, or 83 cents a share, on sales of $1.23 billion, up from year-ago earnings of $51 million, or 69 cents a share, on revenues of $1.17 billion.
Case said the Latin American and Asia Pacific regions had stronger results, which stemmed partly from its acquisitions last year.
Sales of four-wheel drive agricultural tractors jumped 40 percent in the Asia Pacific region, and construction equipment sales were up 35 percent, it said.
Latin American sales of agricultural equipment rose 36 percent, and construction equipment sales were up 53 percent from the first quarter of last year.

In North America, Case said sales of its agricultural equipment were up 6 percent, with gains in four-wheel drive tractors and combines. Construction equipment sales benefited from historically strong housing starts.

In Europe, demand for tractors slowed, but Case said it believes that farm consolidation will drive greater sales of higher-horsepower units. Housing construction in Britain has been brisk, while France and Germany's construction sectors remain weak, Case said.
Case's stock was off 50 cents at $54.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
